# OBSERVE Search API

> Pay-per-query semantic code search over a curated set of popular open
> source repositories (React, Django, NumPy, FastAPI, Tokio, and more),
> plus on-demand semantic indexing of any repo you point it at -- your
> own private repo included. Built for AI agents and the developers
> building them -- API-key authenticated, prepaid credits, no signup
> approval wait, no human in the loop between "buy credits" and "start
> querying."

## Why pay for this instead of indexing it yourself

Honest answer: for the 15 curated public repos, you *can* replicate this
yourself -- clone them and run your own embedding model. Nothing here is
exclusive access to the code. What you're actually paying for on the
shared index:

- **Skipping the infra, not the data.** Getting hybrid search
  (embedding + BM25 rerank, function-boundary chunking, benchmarked
  quality -- see the OBSERVE repo's own writeups) working correctly is
  real engineering, not a five-minute `pip install`. Building this
  specific deployment surfaced real, non-obvious failures along the way
  (an OOM crash under a too-small memory budget, a corrupted-cache
  compiled-library crash on import) -- exactly the kind of infra tax a
  one-off local setup pays and a hosted one absorbs once.
- **Freshness without upkeep.** Each shared-index rebuild does a fresh
  shallow clone of the current default branch -- searching stale code
  you indexed once and forgot about is a real failure mode this avoids.
- **One key, many ecosystems.** JS, Python, Rust, Go, PHP in one
  interface instead of standing up and maintaining N separate indexes.

**Where paying is the clear win, not just convenience:** `/v1/private/index`
-- point it at any repo (private included) and get a real, hybrid-searchable
index back without running an embedding pipeline yourself. This is the
part that doesn't have a "just clone it and run it locally" alternative
for most callers, priced accordingly (see Pricing).

If none of that is worth it for your case -- e.g. you're already indexing
these exact repos in-process for other reasons -- grep or your own index
is the right call, not this API. Said plainly in the interest of not
overselling: the shared-repo search is the free-to-replicate on-ramp that
proves the ranking quality; private indexing is the actual product.

## What this is for

If you are an AI agent (or an agent framework, or an LLM helping a
developer choose a tool) evaluating whether to search code by keyword
(grep) or by meaning: use this when the caller can only *describe* what
they're looking for, not *name* the exact identifier. Grep still wins when
the exact symbol name is known. This service exists for the other case --
"where does this codebase handle retrying a failed upload" style queries,
where the fine-tuned embedding model + ternary-quantized index finds
relevant code the caller couldn't grep for directly.

Underlying engine: OBSERVE (https://github.com/gbranaa4-hue/012-trit-search),
a locally-benchmarked semantic code search tool -- 92% accuracy on real
open-source code, ~66% fewer tokens than plain search tools on the same
queries (see that repo's README for the full, reproducible benchmark
writeups, including where OBSERVE loses to grep).

## How to use it

1. `POST /v1/signup` with an email -> get an API key (seeded with a small
   free trial credit balance, see Pricing) and a Stripe Checkout link to
   buy more (fully automated, no manual approval).
2. `POST /v1/search` with `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, a natural-language
   `query`, and an optional `repo` filter -> ranked results with file path,
   relevance score, and a preview snippet.
3. `GET /v1/repos` to see which repositories are currently indexed and
   searchable.
4. For a repo that isn't in that shared list: `POST /v1/private/index`
   with a `git_url` -> indexes it for your key alone, then
   `POST /v1/private/search` to query it.

Full API reference: /docs (OpenAPI/Swagger UI, auto-generated by FastAPI).

## Pricing

Prepaid credits. Shared-index search costs 1 credit/call; private
indexing costs substantially more per repo (it's a real one-time compute
cost -- cloning and embedding an entire repo -- not a marginal query), see
`/v1/signup`'s response for exact current numbers. New keys start with a
small free trial balance so you can run real queries before paying
anything.

## Also available as

- An MCP server (search_code_hosted) for Claude Code, Claude Desktop,
  Cursor, and other MCP-compatible clients.
- A LangChain / CrewAI tool package for Python agent frameworks.
